text: Harnaam Kaur, born on 29 November 1990, is a British social media personality, postpartum coach, life coach, and motivational speaker. She was born in Slough, Berkshire, in a traditional Punjabi family. At the age of 12, she was diagnosed with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), a condition characterized by elevated androgens in females, which causes hirsutism—the growth of excessive facial and body hair. As a result, Kaur grows a full beard. Initially, she tried to remove her facial hair due to constant bullying, but she has since embraced her appearance and become a spokesperson for the body positivity movement. In an interview with Rock N Roll Bride, she stated, "I decided to keep my beard and step forward against society's expectations of what a woman should look like. Today I am not suicidal and I do not self-harm. Today I am happy living as a young beautiful bearded woman. I have realised that this body is mine, I own it, I do not have any other body to live in so I may as well love it unconditionally." Before gaining media attention, Kaur worked as a primary school teaching assistant at Khalsa Primary School. She began receiving public attention in 2014 and later became a full-time public figure, freelance model, and motivational speaker. In March 2015, photographer Mr. Elbank included her in an exhibit at Somerset House in London featuring over 80 individuals with beards. In June 2015, she modeled for Rock N Roll Bride and was photographed by Louisa Coulthurst of Urban Bridesmaid Photography. In November 2015, she joined the "Eff Your Beauty Standards" campaign founded by Tess Holliday as a spokesperson. In March 2016, she became the first woman with a beard to walk at London Fashion Week, opening the show for designer Marianna Harutunian. She is signed to Wanted Models in Paris and appears in fashion spreads in both online and print magazines. In May 2016, conceptual artist Annelies Hofmeyr featured her in the project Trophy Wife Barbie, altering a Barbie doll to her likeness. In July 2016, musician Aisha Mizra included her in the music video for her song "Fuck Me or Destroy Me." In September 2016, Kaur was included in the Guinness World Records as the youngest woman in the world to have a full beard, with the citation stating: "Now with a beard measuring as long as six inches [15 cm] in places, she overcame years of bullying to take ownership of her appearance and achieve this record title at the age of 24 years 282 days." In March 2017, she was featured in a Teen Vogue article titled "Instagrammers Challenge Body and Facial Hair Stigma." In August 2017, she collaborated with grooming company Captain Fawcett to create and design a beard oil elixir, modeling in the advertisement campaign. In interviews and on social media, Kaur discusses the abuse and harassment she endured as a teenager, which led to self-harm and attempted suicide. In 2017, she participated in panel discussions in the House of Parliament on mental health, body image, cyberbullying, LGBTQIA+, and how social media, businesses, schools, and the government can support positive body images. Kaur uses Instagram, Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube to promote body-positive campaigns, raising awareness about body shaming, cyberbullying, and mental illness, and challenging gender stereotypes in media. She has said, "I don't think I believe in gender. I want to know who said a vagina is for a woman and a penis is for a man, or pink is for a girl and blue is for a boy. I am sitting here with a vagina and boobs – and a big beautiful beard." While she converted to Sikhism at age 16 as a reason for stopping hair removal, she now identifies as spiritual rather than religious. Traditionally, Sikhism forbids cutting hair, so she continues to wear a turban or other head coverings, a practice from the Khalsa tradition. Kaur is originally from Slough, England, and her younger brother, Gurdeep Singh Cheema, created the film Happy Ending? The Dangers of Online Grooming to raise awareness about online child grooming. To promote self-love and acceptance, Kaur named her beard Sundri, meaning beauty or beautiful, and refers to her beard as "she."
